chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ismail ibn Yasar, from Uthman ibn Affan al-Sadusi, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the bathhouse, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you want the bathhouse?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) ordered the bathhouse to be warmed, then entered and wore an izar (garment), covering his knees and navel. Then he ordered the owner of the bathhouse to anoint what was outside the izar, then said: 'Go out from me'. Then he (peace be upon him) anointed what was underneath it with his own hand, then said: 'Thus, do it'.

key_terms.طَلَى: To anoint/smear (with water or oil for purification)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to perform ritual purification when entering a bathhouse according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of maintaining ritual purity (taharah) in public spaces, specifically addressing the concern of impurity transfer from the floor of the bathhouse. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates a methodical approach where the garment is anointed externally before removal, and the body is anointed directly, ensuring that the wearer remains in a state of cleanliness for prayer. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing hygiene with the preservation of ritual validity in daily life.

en.hubeali: A number of our companons, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ismail Bin Yasaar, from Usman Bin Affan Al Sadousy, from Basheer Al Nabaal who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the bathhouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you want to bathing?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered with the warming of the bath, then he<sup>asws</sup> entered it, and he<sup>asws</sup> was wearing a trouser, and his<sup>asws</sup> knees were covered, as well as his<sup>asws</sup> navel. Then he<sup>asws</sup> ordered the one in charge of the bathhouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> anointed what was outside from the trouser. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘go away from me<sup>asws</sup>’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> anointed what was underneath it by his<sup>asws</sup> own hands, then said: ‘This is how, so do it’.
en.sarwar: 21. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar have narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandiy from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn Hammad from abu Maryam al-Ansariy in a marfu‘ manner has said the following:

“Once al-Hassan ibn Ali, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, came out of the bathhouse and someone met him and said, ‘I wish you a fine bathing Istihmam.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You are poor in vocabulary, why does the word ‘’1st’ (meaning your seeking bath or the word’s other meaning which is ‘buttock’) need to be mentioned?’ He then said, ‘I wish you a good ‘Humaym’ . He (the Imam) said, ‘Did you not know that ‘Humaym’ means perspiration?’ He then said, ‘May your bathhouse be nice.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If you wish a nice bathhouse then what is for me in it? You should instead say, ‘I wish purity for what is nice of you and nicety of what is pure of you.’”
